chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'From the preserved sermons of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is that he said: O people! For you there are markers/landmarks, so reach your markers, and for you there is an end/limit, so reach your end. Indeed, the Believer acts between two fears: between a term that has passed, not knowing what Allah will do with it, and between a term that remains, not knowing what Allah has decreed regarding it.'

So let the believing servant take from his self for his self, and from his world for his Hereafter, and in his youth before old age, and in his life before death. And by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, there is no 'time for deeds' (musta'tab) after the world, and there is no abode after it except Paradise or Hellfire.

key_terms.مَخَافَتَيْنِ: two fears (of the past and the future)
key_terms.مُسْتَعْتَبٍ: a period of time for deeds/reprieve
key_terms.نِهَايَةً: an end or limit (the final destination/death)

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet's sermon say about the believer's state between the past and future?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a prophetic sermon highlighting the believer's state of 'fear' (khawf) between the uncertain past and the inevitable future, urging proactive preparation during youth and life. This tradition underscores the Shia concept of balancing hope and fear, emphasizing that death marks the end of the opportunity for deeds, leading directly to either Paradise or Hell.
